assumptions.text: All 6 contexts run in the 1 fleetd process, so every context-to-context message is in-process. Only the command channel, the file protocol, the herdr adapter, the platform layer, git and GitHub cross a process boundary (design: Architecture and roles).

Cross-context events are in-memory events consumed in the level-triggered 5 s reconcile pass, which re-derives work from ledger rows, so a lost event is caught on the next pass. Delivery is at-least-once and every consumer is idempotent on a natural key (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation; decision D1).
Every state change in every flow commits through the single ledger writer in fleet-runtime (decompose N5). The flows do not draw that call on each step.

Operator commands travel as horch CLI requests over the fleetd command channel (Unix socket or named pipe, through the platform layer), drawn as via other. When fleetd is down the request goes to a request file that fleetd reads at start (design: The command channel). Each request carries an idempotency_key, and a refusal carries its reason (orchestrator, D15).

Agent hand-offs (assumptions.md, plan.yaml, result.json, questions, exit.json) are files: atomic, immutable and read in the pass, so they are at-least-once and idempotent on path and content hash (design: Workspace layout and file protocol).

3 message ids were minted here: launch-environment (query), start-agent-process (command) and trial-merge-result (query). Discover adopted all 3 (discover N10): start-agent-process is a discover command, and the 2 queries reuse discover read-model ids.

The fleet-run wrapper belongs to worker-profiles (D2 option B, orchestrator D15). It writes heartbeat.json and exit.json. attempt-exited (exit.json) comes from worker-profiles, the writer of the file; the file records the exit fact of the CLI process.
git is called by 2 contexts, split by concern: worktree-custody for worktrees and rescue refs, integration for branches, merges, bundles and trial merges (orchestrator, D15).

worker-profiles owns start-agent-process (decompose N8). task-execution and ideas send it; worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper and starts it in its own process group through the platform layer. When the profile needs a pane, the caller gets the pane from the herdr adapter of fleet-runtime (R12, R13) and passes it in the request.

Each file of the design workspace layout that crosses the process boundary is 1 message: task.yaml (assign-task), inbox/START.md (start-work), heartbeat.json (heartbeat-written), verdict.json (task-verdict-written), plan.verdict.json (plan-verdict-written) and approval.json (assumptions-approved). The path names its 1 writer (design: Workspace layout and file protocol, rule 3). 6 of these ids are minted here, because discover has no id for them: assign-task, start-work, heartbeat-written, task-verdict-written, plan-verdict-written and agent-status-changed (Q6).
Payload field names are the snake_case names of the design (orchestrator, D15). A file message uses the field names of the design example of that file; an in-memory event uses <entity>_id.
The model has 9 flows, 2 more than the 4 to 7 of depth standard. F2 and F3 were split at a hand-off (F8, F9) to keep each flow at 9 messages or fewer after the new file and pull request messages.

notes_for_downstream.text: All 13 relationships are in-process in 1 deployable. Only these messages cross a process boundary and need a stable contract: operator commands on the command channel, agent and wrapper files (file protocol), start-agent-process (herdr and platform), trial-merge-result and other git calls, and GitHub.

Cross-context events are in-memory and at-least-once through the level-triggered reconcile pass. Every consumer must be idempotent on the key in messages[].idempotency; no outbox table is needed (decision D1).

Sharpens decompose N2 and follows decompose N8: task-execution and ideas send start-agent-process to worker-profiles. worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper (D2 option B) and starts it through the platform layer. Neither ideas nor task-execution builds an environment or starts a process itself.
Sharpens decompose N6: abandon-task-branch must wait for worktree-rescued before the branch is dropped (CC7), and no git call or process start runs inside a ledger transaction (CC6).

D2 option B (orchestrator, D15): the fleet-run wrapper belongs to worker-profiles, not fleet-runtime. It builds the private config home, scrubs the environment, maps CLI events, writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, and calls the platform interface for the process group and kill.
Answers Q4 (orchestrator, D15): task-execution and integration are a partnership. R6 and R7 change together; both directions stay versioned in-memory events (CC1).

9 messages are new and cross a process boundary: assign-task (task.yaml), start-work (START.md), heartbeat-written (heartbeat.json), task-verdict-written (verdict.json), plan-verdict-written (plan.verdict.json), assumptions-approved (approval.json), agent-status-changed (herdr), open-pull-request and pull-request-merged (github).

Contract rules (orchestrator, D15): each command-channel request and request file carries idempotency_key; a refused request returns its reason; result.json status is 1 of completed, blocked, failed; reset_at of usage-limit-reported is optional, and when it is absent fleetd waits until the pool probe reports ok.

decisions.question: How do the co-located contexts deliver a cross-context reaction?

options.summary: In-memory domain events consumed in the level-triggered reconcile pass; the pass re-derives work from ledger rows.
pros: A lost event is caught on the next pass
cons: Up to 5 s latency per hop
risks: A consumer that is not idempotent repeats a side effect

options.summary: A transactional outbox table and a relay inside fleetd, with an inbox for de-duplication.
cons: A second source of truth beside the rows
More code in the single writer

options.summary: Direct synchronous calls between modules inside 1 ledger transaction.
cons: Couples state machines in 1 call stack
External calls end up inside the transaction
risks: A git or process call holds the only writer (CC6)

decisions.rationale: The design settles it: fleetd runs 1 level-triggered reconcile pass every 5 s so a missed event is caught on the next pass (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation). The strongest argument against A: 5 s per hop makes a 4-hop chain such as F2 take up to 20 s.
would_flip_if: Latency of a pass hop becomes visible to the operator
A consumer side effect cannot be made idempotent

decisions.question: Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper, the per-attempt program that writes heartbeat.json and exit.json?

options.summary: task-execution: the wrapper reports attempt facts, and the attempt is a task-execution aggregate.
pros: Heartbeat, lease renewal and exit stay in 1 context
risks: Process details leak into the core model

options.summary: worker-profiles: the wrapper builds the config home and maps CLI events per adapter.
cons: Attempt facts then cross R10 back to task-execution

options.summary: fleet-runtime: the wrapper is process supervision through the platform layer.
cons: fleet-runtime must know CLI event formats
risks: fleet-runtime stops being a thin generic layer (strategize N1)

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. The design names the wrapper as a component but not a context. Recommendation: B, because the wrapper's variable part is per CLI adapter; the strongest argument against it is that heartbeat facts feed the task-execution lease every 10 s. The orchestrator chose B, the recommendation of this step. Reason of the orchestrator: the wrapper is the profile made real (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping), and the scrub needs 1 owner. Process group and kill go through the platform interface, which each context calls. This differs from the recommendation of the code step (fleet-runtime).

1 pull request per feature_id; integration reads features.pr first and does not open a second one
messages.description: after the full gate passes; pr setting gh opens it with gh, manual pushes the feature branch and records the compare URL; a stacked feature uses the lower feature branch as base (design: Features, landing and integration)

messages.idempotency: once per feature_id; check-merged confirms the merge in the primary branch by content before feature-merged
messages.description: the merge fact from GitHub; a manual merge is found by check-merged alone

messages.idempotency: task.yaml is written by fleetd before the launch, atomic and never rewritten; a change is a new attempt
messages.description: task.yaml, written by fleetd from the committed plan (design: Workspace layout and file protocol)

messages.idempotency: 1 inbox/START.md per attempt; the doorbell line that points at it is constant (FM-15)
messages.description: inbox/START.md, what the worker reads first; its path is the launch argument

messages.idempotency: the file is rewritten every 10 s; the highest seq wins and a lower or equal seq is ignored
messages.description: heartbeat.json, written by the fleet-run wrapper (worker-profiles, D2), not the model; an outside signal that renews the lease

messages.idempotency: 1 verdict.json per verified attempt; fleetd is its only writer
messages.description: verdict.json, the decision of the verifier

messages.idempotency: 1 plan.verdict.json per (idea, plan content hash)
messages.description: plan.verdict.json, the result of plan validation; a refusal carries its reasons

messages.idempotency: fleetd writes approval.json only on your approve, with the hash you saw, and ignores any other approval.json (FM-32, I7)
messages.description: approval.json, written by fleetd when you run horch idea approve

messages.idempotency: edge events can be lost by design; each pass re-reads session.snapshot, so a repeat or a loss changes nothing
messages.description: pane.agent_status_changed from the herdr socket events.subscribe, received through the herdr adapter of fleet-runtime (R12, R13): working, blocked on a dialog, or idle

integration_patterns.rationale: Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). In-memory domain events of a versioned type, consumed in the level-triggered reconcile pass (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation).
Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). Events from ideas; task-execution reacts. No caller needs an answer now.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). replan-requested as an in-memory event; the sub-orchestrator does the replan through files.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-leased and the worktree lease row commit in 1 ledger transaction; git worktree add runs after the commit (decompose R4, CC5).
Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). worktree-created and rescue-failed as in-memory events read in the next pass.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-done and task-escalated as in-memory events; integration hosts mark-branch-ready. R6 and R7 are a partnership (orchestrator, D15): they change together.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened as in-memory events; task-execution launches the attempt. R6 and R7 are a partnership (orchestrator, D15).

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-branch-landed as an in-memory event; worktree-custody refuses a removal that loses work (04 W6).
Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-branch-landed and feature-merged as in-memory events; ideas never reads git.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). task-execution sends start-agent-process to worker-profiles, which owns the environment scrub and the fleet-run wrapper (decompose N8, D2). task-execution asks launch-environment synchronously only to check a fallback persona (F4). heartbeat.json comes back as a file.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). ideas sends start-agent-process to worker-profiles for a sub-orchestrator pane (F1), with the same environment scrub.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). Calls through the fleet-runtime facade: the single ledger writer (decompose N5) and the herdr adapter, which gives panes and delivers agent-status-changed. Process starts go through worker-profiles, not fleet-runtime. No flow draws a step to fleet-runtime: the ledger writer sits under every step (A3), and the flows draw the herdr adapter as herdr itself.

Both contexts are code inside the 1 fleetd process (design: Architecture and roles; scale target 1 deployable). The same facade for ideas: the command channel delivers horch idea commands and the answers of the sub-orchestrator, and the herdr adapter gives sub-orchestrator panes. No flow draws a step to fleet-runtime: the ledger writer sits under every step (A3), and the flows draw the herdr adapter as herdr itself.

coupling_concerns.text: task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Keep both directions as versioned in-memory events only, never direct calls. The orchestrator (D15) declared R6 and R7 a partnership: the 2 contexts plan their changes together (answers Q4).

coupling_concerns.text: ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Accepted: decompose split the 2 directions into R2 and R3 on purpose. Both directions stay events.

coupling_concerns.text: ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Accepted: R1 and R9 are both published languages; ideas never reads git and integration never reads idea files.

coupling_concerns.text: task-execution and worktree-custody depend on each other (R4 and R5): the worktree lifecycle follows the task lease and the attempt end, and launch waits for the worktree.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Accepted as the lifecycle link of decompose N6; keep it as events in both directions.

coupling_concerns.text: task-leased is an event, but task-execution cannot launch until the worktree exists, and a failed git worktree add must come back to task-execution. The event hides a command that needs a result.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: task-execution acts as the process manager of dispatch: lease and worktree lease row in 1 transaction, then create-worktree, then launch on worktree-created, with a timeout back to ready.

coupling_concerns.text: Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Commit, then call, then record the outcome as an event in the next pass; never call git or start a process while the ledger transaction is open.

coupling_concerns.text: abandon-task-branch drops a task branch in integration, but the rescue ref that keeps the work is made in worktree-custody (04 W6). Both must happen, in order, or work is lost.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: integration asks worktree-custody to rescue first and drops the branch only on worktree-rescued; integration owns this process.

coupling_concerns.text: plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Keep the policy in task-execution only for a replan of an existing task; a refused first plan stays in ideas. ideas owns the 1 needs-you list (orchestrator, D15), so task-escalated goes back to ideas (F6).

coupling_concerns.text: task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.
coupling_concerns.mitigation: Keep 1 thin event (branch, task_id, feature_id, tip); each consumer reads its own rows.

plain_words.what: We drew how the 6 parts of fleetd pass work to each other, in 9 step-by-step flows and 51 named messages.
plain_words.decided: All 6 parts run in 1 program, so they talk by in-memory messages that a 5-second loop re-checks. Only the operator's commands, the agents' files, herdr, git, GitHub and process starts leave the program. worker-profiles starts every agent process.
plain_words.assumed: We assumed a lost in-memory message is harmless because the loop re-reads the database every 5 seconds and redoes missing work.
plain_words.riskiest: If a part reacts twice to the same message and is not built to ignore the repeat, it can launch a worker twice or open 2 features for 1 idea.
